patterns.title: Declaration and definition chronology can change GC/1.3.2 output
patterns.summary: Moving file-scope definitions earlier can change one-pass visibility, register allocation, section extents, and relocations even when the C declarations appear equivalent.
patterns.conditions: Apply as a compiler-wide diagnostic under GC/1.3.2; probe each owner locally because stage.c is a counterexample to the mdparty tail-definition requirement.

source_condition.change: Move file-scope object definitions earlier or otherwise alter declaration/definition chronology while retaining nominally equivalent declarations.

known_signatures: a semantics-preserving reorder regresses many exact functions
section extent changes without an intentional data-layout change

patterns.rule: Treat declaration chronology as a testable compiler variable; do not modernize definition placement or copy a tail-definition layout without owner-local proof.
safe_actions: make a bounded owner-local chronology probe
compare every independently exact function and affected data section
record both positive and negative owner results
counterexamples: REL:mdpartydll:stage

patterns.title: Keep mdparty same-owner definitions at the authenticated tail position
patterns.summary: mdparty.c requires declarations before code and the same-owner definitions at the translation-unit tail to retain the retail text, BSS, and relocation chronology.
patterns.conditions: This is specific to REL:mdpartydll:mdparty and must not be copied to stage.c or another owner.

source_condition.change: Move one or more mdparty-owned object definitions before application code or regroup the authenticated reverse tail order.

known_signatures: early-definition probe retained only 154 of 258 exact functions
source text and BSS extents diverged from retail

patterns.rule: Preserve the authenticated mdparty declaration-before-code and reverse tail-definition chronology unless stronger same-game evidence disproves it.
safe_actions: leave the existing tail chronology intact during semantic cleanup
test any ownership cleanup in an isolated probe before retaining it
verify the complete relocation stream after data-definition changes
counterexamples: REL:mdpartydll:stage

patterns.title: A broader correct header can still produce the wrong translation-unit output
patterns.summary: Adding semantically correct declarations through a broad header can change emitted calls, temporary lifetimes, allocation, and inline behavior when the retail translation unit saw a narrower declaration set.
patterns.conditions: Use as a compiler-wide diagnostic; local prototypes are acceptable only when symbol authority and an owner-specific visibility probe support them.

source_condition.change: Replace target-visible local prototypes with a broad owner header or add declarations that were not visible in the retail translation unit.
requires: the include changes the visible declaration set

known_signatures: one exact caller becomes eight bytes shorter
several independently exact functions diverge after a header-only cleanup

patterns.rule: Do not treat broader modern header visibility as historically authentic merely because the declarations are correct; reproduce and test the retail translation-unit visibility.
safe_actions: compare the preprocessed declaration set before and after the include
run an owner-local broad-header probe
retain narrow local declarations only with symbol authority and recorded evidence

patterns.title: Retain the target-visible mdparty audio declarations without the broad audio header
patterns.summary: fn_1_2F22C is exact only when mdparty sees the four authenticated local audio declarations rather than the complete audio header.
patterns.conditions: Applies to the authenticated mdparty translation-unit visibility; it is not a general license for duplicate local prototypes.

source_condition.change: Include game/audio.h in mdparty.c or otherwise expose the full audio declaration set to fn_1_2F22C.

known_signatures: fn_1_2F22C becomes eight bytes shorter with the broad header

patterns.rule: Keep the four policy-checked local audio declarations and do not include the broad audio header in mdparty.c without new target evidence.
safe_actions: keep signatures mirrored against the authoritative audio header
let the declaration-ownership gate detect drift
re-run fn_1_2F22C and its caller evidence after any audio contract change

patterns.title: Retain stage's authenticated signed random prototypes
patterns.summary: stage.c requires its target-backed signed frandmod and rand8 declarations; broad random-function headers change five exact functions.
patterns.conditions: Specific to REL:mdpartydll:stage and its retail declaration visibility.

source_condition.change: Replace stage's local signed frandmod/rand8 prototypes with a broader random-function header.

known_signatures: broad random visibility reduces source text from the retail extent and diverges five functions

patterns.rule: Keep the two target-backed signed local prototypes in stage.c unless stronger same-game evidence authenticates broader visibility.
safe_actions: keep symbol authority in the declaration policy
compare all 57 stage functions after random-contract changes
do not copy this exception to another owner

patterns.title: Check helper boundaries and object lifetimes before adding code-generation controls
patterns.summary: Real helper boundaries, automatic inline decisions, narrow contracts, and block-scoped lifetimes can explain repeated register and control-flow mismatches across related callers.
patterns.conditions: Use when the same mismatch family appears around calls, saved registers, temporary elimination, or nested control flow; a single isolated match is insufficient.

source_condition.change: Flatten or recreate helpers, widen a narrow contract, or move a temporary outside its likely original block scope.
requires: a repeated mismatch family across related call sites
target or sibling evidence for the helper or contract

known_signatures: multiple callers close together after restoring one helper family
a block-scope or signed-contract correction removes one repeated temporary

patterns.rule: Before using pragmas or artificial expressions, test the authenticated helper boundary, narrow type contract, and block lifetime that could naturally produce the mismatch family.
safe_actions: compare the same helper pattern across all known callers
test signedness and scope independently
retain the change only when related callers improve without exact regressions

patterns.title: Recover narrow signed contracts from target and consumer widths before widening to int
patterns.summary: Signed-short parameters and returns can change extension nodes, temporary lifetimes, branches, and wrapped allocator chronology even when an int signature appears semantically equivalent.
patterns.conditions: Use as a compiler-wide type diagnostic when callers, symbol data, or target instructions show 16-bit signed movement or extension.

source_condition.change: Widen an s16 argument or return contract to int, or insert casts that erase the original signed-short node.

known_signatures: an exact body closes only after restoring an s16 return
multiple inline boundaries share the same signed argument-node difference

patterns.rule: Choose narrow signed types from target and consumer evidence, not from modern convenience or one function's isolated code generation.
safe_actions: inspect caller and consumer widths before changing the signature
compare extension instructions at every boundary
re-test all Matching consumers of a shared declaration

patterns.title: Pin independent same-game source by commit and blob before using it
patterns.summary: The mariopartyrd MP6 repository is same-game evidence with an independent Git history; it can authenticate retained contracts and source hypotheses, but it cannot be merged or treated as a newer ancestor.
patterns.conditions: Apply whenever source, headers, symbols, catalogs, or configuration are consulted from an independent repository for the same retail target.

source_condition.change: Adopt a name, type, layout, source shape, or configuration value from an independent same-game repository.
requires: pinned repository commit and path blob
matching target region or consumer contract
current-toolchain object and relocation validation for emitted code

known_signatures: the donor has no merge base with human main
a retained source blob is labeled Matching without committed object or relocation proof

patterns.rule: Treat a pinned independent same-game blob as high-value evidence, never as merge authority; target instructions, relocations, sections, consumers, and the current retail build remain decisive.
safe_actions: record repository, commit, path, blob, and introducing commit
extract only the contract or source hypothesis needed by the active owner
rebuild and compare the active object before accepting emitted-code claims

patterns.title: A configured Matching label is a claim until retail proof is replayed
patterns.summary: The pinned same-game repository labels 54 owners Matching but commits no object reports, relocation reports, or replayable checksum proof; current acceptance must regenerate those dimensions.
patterns.conditions: Apply to imported status labels, historical progress reports, cached objdiff output, and source blobs from any branch or repository.

source_condition.change: Treat a historical Matching or Equivalent label as sufficient evidence for current integration.
requires: linked retail checksum when integration is claimed

known_signatures: source blobs differ while both repositories label an owner Matching
no reproducible object or checksum artifact accompanies the label

patterns.rule: Report configured status separately from freshly replayed retained-object, relocation, section, and linked-output results.
safe_actions: compile the active object in an isolated current worktree
save a fresh relocation-aware objdiff report
run the serialized linked hash gate before integration completion

patterns.title: Resolve the final compiler profile from the emitted TU command
patterns.summary: MP6 uses multiple MWCC versions and layered flag profiles; the same nominal compiler family can emit under different terminal optimization, pooling, small-data, and ABI options.
patterns.conditions: Apply before source-shape tuning, donor comparison, or any claim that a compiler probe represents retail.

source_condition.change: Infer a translation unit's effective compiler flags from a base profile, sibling owner, or earlier duplicate option instead of its final generated command.
requires: generated command with later options resolved

known_signatures: O0 and O4 controls change vector helpers from compact inlined bodies to much larger output
GC/1.3.2 REL owners require sdata, sdata2, and pool controls absent from game owners

patterns.rule: Pin and report compiler bundle, executable hash, owner class, complete generated command, final duplicate-option semantics, linker, and region before interpreting a source mismatch.
safe_actions: inspect the exact Ninja command for the active object
run one untouched-source compiler control when the brief and generated command conflict
reject a compiler profile that regresses independently exact functions

patterns.title: A same-address API alias does not prove the original source spelling
patterns.summary: GXInitLightAttnA and GXInitLightAttnK resolve to the same MP6 target address, proving ABI aliasing but not which SDK spelling appeared in the original source.
patterns.conditions: Apply when maps, symbol files, headers, or sibling repositories expose multiple names for one target address.

source_condition.change: Rename a call, export, global, or field solely because another same-address alias emits identical code.
requires: independent naming provenance for source spelling

known_signatures: two SDK names relocate to main:0x800B392C
binary equality cannot distinguish the source token

patterns.rule: Preserve the established exported/API spelling unless maps, exports, SDK provenance, or stronger same-game evidence authenticates the alternative; record byte equality and naming confidence separately.
safe_actions: retain owner plus address as the stable identity
verify both aliases have the same prototype and relocation target
record alternate names as aliases rather than silently renaming source

patterns.title: Use same-game headers for ABI widths without inheriting unproved semantic names
patterns.summary: Independent MP6 headers and Matching-owner consumers provide strong width, callback, array-dimension, and offset evidence even when alternate field and function names disagree.
patterns.conditions: Use when reconstructing prototypes, callback classes, struct layouts, array extents, or compact state fields from same-game retained headers.

source_condition.change: Adopt a same-game header contract or semantic field name into an active owner.
requires: target access width and offset checks

known_signatures: charman headers expose s16, u8, GX callback, and GW_CHARA_MAX contracts
different GW_PLAYER bitfield names retain the same byte offsets and widths

patterns.rule: Adopt mechanically corroborated ABI widths and layouts first; keep semantic names provisional until behavior, exports, maps, or assets authenticate them.
safe_actions: verify offsetof, sizeof, access width, and every consumer
preserve fn_/lbl_ or established API names when semantic provenance is weaker
record layout confidence independently from naming confidence

patterns.title: Keep same-game asset catalogs target-specific and verify every archive index
patterns.summary: The independent MP6 repository preserves motion, message, minigame, and sound catalogs, but their numeric domains remain target-specific and require archive or table verification before use.
patterns.conditions: Apply when naming or generating datanum, message, sound, movie, DLL, or resource constants.

source_condition.change: Adopt a numeric asset, message, sound, or datanum constant from a retained catalog.
requires: every index verified against archive/table order

known_signatures: filename suffixes need not equal archive indices
a sibling-game catalog can be structurally similar but numerically wrong

patterns.rule: Use pinned MP6 catalogs only within their recorded domain, regenerate repetitive enums from actual MP6 archives where possible, and never transfer numeric catalogs between games.
safe_actions: record catalog path, blob, owning archive/table, count, and verification method
generate rather than manually transcribe repetitive enums
reject an index inferred only from a filename suffix

patterns.title: Treat the upstream board bulk rename as mapping provenance, not semantic proof
patterns.summary: The independent repository records the same 2,021 board address-to-name pairs as current main, introduced by one bulk rename without per-symbol authentication records.
patterns.conditions: Apply when evaluating an established semantic board name whose only located provenance is the upstream bulk rename.

source_condition.change: Treat an address-to-name mapping from commit 7a463aa as proof that the spelling came from retail source or exports.
requires: independent map, export, caller, asset, or sibling evidence for semantic confidence

known_signatures: all 2,021 mappings are identical across independent histories
the rename commit contains no per-name evidence ledger

patterns.rule: Preserve established public board names for compatibility, but cite the bulk rename only as mapping history and seek separate evidence before calling a semantic name authenticated.
safe_actions: retain owner plus address as stable identity
record mapping provenance separately from semantic confidence
do not churn established exported names during body recovery

patterns.title: Select the authenticated owner-local GC/2.6 sqrtf header before changing board literals
patterns.summary: For a GC/2.6 board owner whose generic math closure emits source-only `_half` and `_three` sqrtf statics, an authenticated translation-unit selection of the canonical `dolphin/math.h` implementation can remove the 16-byte `.sdata2` prefix and close otherwise instruction-identical SDA21 relocation rows. Gate and roulette close completely, while tutorial and dice gain five strict functions each. Star proves the signature is diagnostic rather than universally corrective, and changing the shared top-level header is unsafe because it regresses exact REL consumers.
patterns.conditions: Use only for a main-board owner under its pinned GC/2.6 command when strict objdiff rows differ at SDA21 literals, value-aware bytes and resolved addresses agree, raw `.sdata2` shows exactly the source-only `_half`/`_three` prefix, and same-game exact translation units authenticate the owner-local header chronology. Require the public quality gate and a whole-project retail build.

source_condition.change: A translation unit selects generic `math.h` or the canonical `dolphin/math.h` sqrtf implementation, changing whether weak function-local `_half` and `_three` statics own the first 16 bytes of `.sdata2`.

possible_changes: later constant-pool offsets and anonymous relocation identities
strict match percentages without instruction or resolved-value changes
unrelated exact REL regressions if the shared top-level header is changed globally
known_signatures: candidate `.sdata2` begins with 8-byte `_half` and 8-byte `_three` local statics absent from retail
SDA21 mismatches resolve to identical float or double bytes under data-value comparison
removing one direct math include is neutral because another header keeps the same transitive closure
gate closes 7/11 to 11/11 and 168/168 relocations after authenticated owner-local header selection
roulette closes 12/21 to 21/21 and 291/291 relocations after the same owner-local selection
tutorial rises 39/55 to 44/55 strict functions with zero exact losses
dice rises 39/68 to 44/68 strict functions with zero exact losses

patterns.rule: Before tuning literals or declaration lifetimes, prove whether transitive sqrtf visibility introduced the `_half`/`_three` pool. Prefer a narrowly authenticated owner-local selection of the existing canonical header, reviewed through a path-specific quality exception; never fabricate constants, pad sections, or change the shared top-level header to solve one owner.
safe_actions: compare strict and data-value relocation reports
inspect the preprocessed include closure and raw `.sdata2` prefix
test only an authenticated owner-local include chronology change
require a path-specific reviewed quality exception for an include-guard override
run every configured retail output after any shared-header diagnostic
record a value-resolved function honestly when relocation spelling alone remains
counterexamples: Removing the direct humath include from main:board/dice was byte-neutral because transitive headers still exposed sqrtf.
Changing shared include/math.h from static to automatic locals improved gate and roulette but regressed seven exact REL outputs, so the global change was reverted.
The authenticated owner-local header selection was byte-neutral for main:board/star at 60/90 strict functions; its early SignMdlTbl chronology and map-view frame mismatch are independent.

patterns.title: Separate DTK gap extents from meaningful source-owned data
patterns.summary: Strictly exact owners can retain target/source section-size differences when DTK exposes linker gaps, alignment tails, final-symbol extents, or discarded targetless pools that are not C object bytes.
patterns.conditions: Apply only after every named source-owned object, function, and effective relocation is exact and a current linked retail checksum proves that the residual bytes do not affect shipped output.

source_condition.change: Interpret a raw section-size or synthetic-symbol extent difference as a missing or incorrectly typed C object.
requires: target and source symbol-table ownership inspection

known_signatures: target-only `.hidden gap_*` symbol covers the residual bytes
a final DTK symbol extent runs beyond the authenticated source type while all uses and linked bytes are exact
source-only header constants have no target symbol or effective relocation and are discarded at link

patterns.rule: Classify ownership at named-object and effective-relocation boundaries; never add padding, widen a real declaration, or retain targetless constants solely to equalize raw section extents.
safe_actions: inspect target and source symbol tables before changing C data
compare named object bytes and effective relocations rather than top-level section percentages alone
require the serialized retail hash gate before calling a gap harmless
record gap-only residuals separately from meaningful data mismatches
counterexamples: A size difference inside a named object, a nonexact effective relocation, or linked-output drift is meaningful and cannot be dismissed as a gap.

patterns.title: Separate MWCC source chronology from final csect link order
patterns.summary: An authenticated inline cluster may need early compiler visibility to seed the retail literal pool even when its machine code belongs later in the linked text order; dedicated csects preserve both dimensions.
patterns.conditions: Use only when complete same-game code and literal chronology authenticate the early owner, every moved function is instruction-identical, and retail function boundaries identify the later text position.

source_condition.change: Move an authenticated function cluster earlier in the translation unit while retaining its machine code at a later retail address.
requires: pinned owner compiler and linker commands
complete instruction-identical cluster and retail function boundaries
file-qualified csect selectors and a final linked retail comparison

known_signatures: instructions are exact but pooled literals follow first-use rather than target prefix order
an unqualified wildcard inserts a later object between owner csects
source csects are independently exact but the linked REL text order is wrong

patterns.rule: Compile the authenticated cluster in literal-owner chronology under dedicated code csects, then concatenate file-qualified owner csects and later objects in retail order; accept the arrangement only after exact sections, relocations, REL bytes, and the full retail gate.
safe_actions: prove the complete cluster and literal chronology across retail evidence
split only at authenticated retail function boundaries
place file-qualified csect selectors before wildcard selectors
replay object, relocation, consumer, REL, DOL, and checksum gates
counterexamples: An unqualified *(.text) selector placed runtime text before the deferred owner csect and failed final layout.
Moving strong definitions without authenticated csect boundaries changes final text order rather than solving pool ownership.
An invented uncalled constant seeder duplicates the pool and is not an authenticated chronology owner.

patterns.title: Authenticate weak extern-inline local-static ownership before using it to explain a pool prefix
patterns.summary: Under the pinned profile, C++ extern-inline function-local static constants can emit weak inactive rodata at zero active-text cost, and the linker may retain the first copy while deduplicating later copies.
patterns.conditions: Apply when a target literal prefix precedes every active reference and compiler controls or sibling RELs show weak inactive local-static emission under the exact profile.

source_condition.change: Expose or reorder an extern-inline body containing function-local static constants.
requires: exact preprocessed inline body and compiler command
authenticated source ownership beyond a capability-only probe

possible_changes: weak inactive rodata with no active text
known_signatures: control object has .text 0 and nonzero rodata with weak inactive constants
linked sibling objects retain only the earliest compatible copy
ordinary unused inline literals emit no corresponding block

patterns.rule: Use weak extern-inline local-static emission as a pool-ownership explanation only after authenticating the real header or shared owner and replaying multi-object link behavior; a synthetic no-text seeder proves capability, not provenance.
safe_actions: inspect weak symbols, active bits, csects, and relocations
compile the real included inline header under the exact compiler profile
compare first-copy retention and dedup across sibling RELs
require exact linked sections and retail bytes
counterexamples: Ordinary unused inline literals emitted nothing under the same profile.
Real MP5 board-math extern-inline bodies did not emit the required MP6 prefix.
A synthetic 19-static header emitted the prefix at zero text cost but duplicated the active bodies' pool and did not authenticate ownership.

patterns.title: Triangulate a missing inline owner from complete sibling retail chronology
patterns.summary: When a historical inline header is absent, a complete byte-identical function cluster plus the same literal prefix and chronology in multiple same-game retail RELs can authenticate shared ownership more strongly than a value-only match.
patterns.conditions: Use only when no surviving same-game source/header authenticates the owner and at least two independent retail modules provide complete code, size-sequence, literal-prefix, and chronology agreement.

source_condition.change: Infer a missing shared inline owner from sibling retail modules rather than a surviving source file.
requires: current-owner instruction, relocation, section, and linked proof

possible_changes: shared-owner confidence without semantic naming proof
known_signatures: multiple retail RELs share a complete cluster hash and size sequence
the same RELs share an earlier literal prefix explained by cluster chronology
multiset-only controls cannot distinguish ownership

patterns.rule: Treat complete cross-module code identity, function boundaries, literal-prefix identity, and literal chronology as a bounded ownership proof; do not infer an owner from matching values or a synthetic emitter alone.
safe_actions: hash complete target clusters across sibling RELs
compare exact prefix bytes and function-size chronology
map each retained literal to an authenticated body
require an organic reconstructed owner and exact retail replay
counterexamples: A matching literal multiset without matching code chronology is not owner proof.
A synthetic no-text seeder that reproduces bytes is not an authenticated source owner.
Ordinary-literal extern-inline functions may deduplicate to an existing tail without seeding the target prefix.

patterns.title: Use literal multisets and direct consumers before moving a DTK rodata boundary
patterns.summary: A one-word rodata size mismatch beside a configured TU boundary may be internal pool order/alignment drift rather than missing data or a misplaced split; literal multisets, direct boundary consumers, and an independently exact adjacent owner distinguish the cases.
patterns.conditions: Apply to PowerPC REL objects when target and source differ near a DTK rodata boundary and the neighboring owner can be built and compared independently.

source_condition.change: Move a DTK rodata split to absorb or release one alignment word near an object boundary.
requires: target/source section sizes and 32-bit literal multisets
direct relocation consumers of boundary symbols
independently exact adjacent-owner section and alignment
build-local boundary probes and final linked proof

possible_changes: DTK split validity without changing literal values
known_signatures: target/source literal multisets agree except one zero alignment word
a proposed earlier boundary leaves a directly referenced symbol unresolved
a proposed later boundary bisects the adjacent owner's exact constant object

patterns.rule: Do not move a DTK rodata boundary from size pressure alone; first prove literal membership, direct consumers, and adjacent-owner ownership, then accept a boundary only if object, relocation, REL, and full checksum gates remain exact.
safe_actions: compare section sizes and 32-bit literal multisets
audit relocations that name the boundary symbol
build the adjacent owner independently
test alternate boundaries only in ignored build-local configs
counterexamples: Moving the w01 boundary to 0x43C left lbl_1_rodata_43C consumers unresolved.
Moving it to 0x444 bisected runtime __constants and DTK rejected the split.
A boundary move that only relabels padding is not ownership proof.

patterns.title: Require conversion-pool relocation ownership before retaining exact text
patterns.summary: MWCC can reproduce every instruction byte in an integer-to-floating conversion function while binding its synthesized literal to a TU-local pool instead of the retail object's separate or preceding owner.
patterns.conditions: Apply when function size and instructions are exact but one or more conversion-literal relocations name a compiler-local symbol instead of the target owner.

source_condition.change: Recover a conversion consumer without the authenticated preceding literal owner or translation-unit chronology.
requires: pinned compiler command and pool profile

possible_changes: correct instructions with incorrect relocation targets
downstream pool offsets that depend on an earlier owner
known_signatures: text is byte-identical while a target lbl_* relocation becomes source @NNN
pool_data off does not suppress the synthesized conversion constant
an equivalent weak named constant coexists with rather than absorbs the anonymous pool
restoring an authenticated preceding owner is expected to move the downstream pool naturally

patterns.rule: Do not retain a text-exact function until its conversion-pool relocation owner is exact; restore authenticated source chronology or keep the function unresolved, and never fabricate a literal, ABI construction, split, or object rewrite to force the symbol name.
safe_actions: compare relocation target symbols in addition to instruction bytes
compile the authenticated preceding-function cluster under the exact profile
test pool_data and named-constant controls only as bounded counterexamples
require organic source and linked consumer proof before retention
examples: s02Dll fn_1_4B8: 0x470 exact text, target lbl_1_rodata_60 versus source @373
s03Dll fn_1_1238: 536 exact text bytes, target lbl_1_rodata_A0 versus source @360
counterexamples: A matching literal value does not prove relocation ownership.
#pragma pool_data off did not suppress the openingDll conversion pool.
A weak equivalent named constant emitted alongside the anonymous pool instead of absorbing it.

patterns.title: Separate narrow assignment semantics from the stored lifetime width
patterns.summary: A semantically narrow API result can require an s32 field or local initialized through an explicit s16 cast so MWCC emits sign extensions at the retail consumer sites.
patterns.conditions: Apply when target code sign-extends a narrow-producing call result and repeats extsh at later consumers, while an s16 source lifetime removes or reschedules those extensions.

source_condition.change: Declare the stored lifetime itself as s16 instead of storing an explicitly narrowed value in an s32 lifetime.
requires: target extension at assignment or first use

known_signatures: an s16 lifetime turns repeated target extsh instructions into mr
an explicit narrow cast at assignment plus s32 storage restores consumer extensions
producer semantics remain narrow even though storage is wide

patterns.rule: Choose storage width from the complete producer-to-consumer instruction pattern; when authenticated, store the explicitly narrowed result in an s32 lifetime rather than declaring the lifetime s16, and retain it only after every extension site and relocation is exact.
safe_actions: authenticate the producer contract before changing the lifetime
compare s16 storage against s32 storage with an explicit narrow assignment cast
inspect every consumer rather than one extsh site
require exact object and relocation proof
counterexamples: A lone extsh without repeated producer/consumer evidence does not authenticate wide storage.
Changing the authoritative API return type to s32 is not implied by an s32 local lifetime.

patterns.title: Use explicit value captures only when GC/2.6 O0 lifetime evidence repeats
patterns.summary: Under the board GC/2.6 -O0,p profile, repeated reads of globals or bitfields can shorten or merge value lifetimes; source-authentic captures at distinct use boundaries can restore the target's saved-register and signed-comparison shape.
patterns.conditions: Use only for a repeated owner-local mismatch family involving global or bitfield reads, saved registers, or signed comparisons; a convenient temporary by itself is not evidence.

source_condition.change: Capture a global or bitfield value at the control-flow point where the target appears to begin its lifetime, rather than sharing one broad temporary or repeatedly folding the expression.
requires: GC/2.6 with the same -O0,p board profile
repeated target evidence for distinct value lifetimes
natural source semantics without register-pressure shaping

known_signatures: the target reloads one global or bitfield at multiple semantic use boundaries
a value becomes live only after an earlier short-circuit check
explicit pointer truthiness restores the target compare sequence

patterns.rule: Treat explicit captures as a bounded owner-local lifetime probe, not a source template; retain them only when strict object and relocation evidence improves without exact regressions.
safe_actions: identify the first target instruction that makes each value live
test captures one semantic boundary at a time
compare every previously exact function in the owner
revert capture or return-shape probes that merely move mismatches
counterexamples: A simplified mbPlayerMoveMain lifetime regressed and was reverted.
Capsule inline return-shape probes regressed and were reverted.
BiriQ relocation-identity residuals are not value-lifetime evidence.
